statement: Consider an arrangement of \(n\) tokens in the plane (not necessarily at distinct points). A move consists of selecting two tokens at points \(A\) and \(B\) and moving both to the midpoint of \(AB\). Call an arrangement collapsible if some finite sequence of moves results in all \(n\) tokens at the same point. Prove that every arrangement of \(n\) tokens is collapsible if and only if \(n\) is a power of \(2\).

Let five points on a circle be labelled \(A, B, C, D, E\) in clockwise order. Assume \(AE = DE\) and let \(P\) be the intersection of \(AC\) and \(BD\). Let \(Q\) be the point on line \(AB\) such that \(A\) is between \(B\) and \(Q\) and \(AQ = DP\). Let \(R\) be the point on line \(CD\) such that \(D\) is between \(C\) and \(R\) and \(DR = AP\). Prove that \(PE \perp QR\).

Two positive integers \(a\) and \(b\) are prime-related if \(a = pb\) or \(b = pa\) for some prime \(p\). Find all positive integers \(n\) such that \(n\) has at least three divisors and all the divisors of \(n\) can be arranged in a circle (without repetition) so that any two adjacent divisors are prime-related.

Find all polynomials \(p(x)\) with real coefficients having the property that there exists a polynomial \(q(x)\) with real coefficients such that
\[p(1) + p(2) + p(3) + \cdots + p(n) = p(n)q(n)\]
for all positive integers \(n\).

Let \(k\) be a given even positive integer. Sarah picks a positive integer \(N > 1\) and each minute chooses a prime divisor \(p\) of the current \(N\) and multiplies \(N\) by \(p^k - p^{-1}\) to get the next value. Prove that there are infinitely many even positive integers \(k\) such that, no matter what choices Sarah makes, her number \(N\) will at some point be divisible by \(2018\).
